Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of characterization and plot shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.) Exemplar: The return of Bingley and Darcy turns the family's ignorance into painful dramatic irony. When the text says “Elizabeth particularly, who knew that her mother owed to the latter the preservation of her favourite daughter from irremediable infamy, was hurt and distressed to a most painful degree by a distinction so ill applied” (Chapter LIII, paragraph 41), it shows this directly. Mrs. Bennet greets Darcy coldly, but Elizabeth knows "her mother owed to the latter the preservation of her favourite daughter from irremediable infamy," so the reader feels the injustice of "a distinction so ill applied."
